asks: should I roam
can I leave lane
do I go help bot
is it time to roam
roam or stay mid
say: Shove the wave into their tower first, then walk to whichever side lane is pushed up, or stay for plates if neither one is.
more: A wave crashed into their tower makes their mid choose between following you and losing minions. Leave on a wave in the middle of the lane and you pay for both.
A roam that only burns a Flash still sets up the next visit, by you or your jungler, a few minutes later.
If nothing is on offer in the side lanes, plates and a clean recall are a fine use of the same push.
check: Where your wave is, whether an enemy side laner is past the middle of his lane, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If your wave is not at their tower, or both side lanes are sitting under their own towers, do not go. Keep farming and look again next wave.
basis: pro:The lane that pushes first moves first

when: dragon or grubs are alive or spawn within about a minute
asks: do I roam top or bot
which lane do I go to
bot or top
who do I help
which side should I roam
say: Go toward the objective that's up next: bot for dragon, top for grubs, or the lane whose enemy has no Flash if you saw it used.
more: A kill beside an objective turns into that objective. A kill on the far side is only a kill, and your jungler may be alone at the pit while you are away.
Bot usually has two targets and two allies with crowd control, so the roam fails less often. Top is a longer wait for a single target.
If both sides look equal, go where your jungler is, so the play is three people and not two.
check: Which side your jungler is on, which enemy laners are pushed up, and whose Flash you actually saw go down.
breaks: If the lane beside the objective is under its own tower, there is no target. Walk into river with your jungler for vision or take plates.

asks: what do I lose if I roam
is roaming worth it
am I throwing by leaving lane
how much does a roam cost me
say: A roam costs you about a wave and maybe a plate, so go for a likely kill, or stay if it's only a maybe.
more: The price is paid in minions and experience. If their mid stays and farms, he can reach his next level or item before you do.
The return is a kill, a burned Flash or an objective. A Flash is worth it if someone comes back to use the window; nothing at all is a straight loss.
Shoving first shrinks the price, because the minions die to their tower either way while he is busy catching them.
check: How large the next wave coming at you is, and how far forward the side lane you want really is.
breaks: If you are already behind their mid in CS or level, the cost is too high. Farm, and let the fights come to river beside you.

asks: their mid is gone do I follow
mid missing what do I do
should I chase him or push
he roamed do I go too
enemy mid left lane
say: Ping it, then shove and take plates so his roam costs him, or follow only if you can get there before he does.
more: Following a few steps behind is the worst of both: you lose the wave and still arrive second, sometimes into a brush he is waiting in.
Plates and a wave lost under his tower can outweigh a kill, and they are guaranteed. That is how you stay even through his roams.
If he roams every time the wave crashes, start shoving later so the wave sits in the middle and he has to leave it.
check: Which way he walked, whether your side lanes have backed off after the ping, and whether the path you would follow through is warded.
breaks: If your side lane is already fighting and you are closer than he is, go at once; an extra body there is worth more than a plate.

when: their mid laner is dead and no objective is alive
asks: I killed mid where do I go
their mid is dead should I roam
he's dead do I go bot
mid is dead now what
say: While he's dead, crash the wave and walk to a side lane or their jungle with your jungler, or recall on the crash to buy.
more: His death timer is the only time you can leave mid for free. Nobody can follow you and nobody can punish the lane.
Crash the wave first so the tower takes his minions. Then he comes back a wave behind as well as a kill behind.
If the side lanes are safe under tower, the recall is the better use: an item lead on his return makes the next kill easier.
check: His respawn timer against how long the walk is, and whether a side lane target is actually reachable.
breaks: If the timer is nearly done, do not start a long walk. Take the plate and recall so you meet him in lane with the item.
basis: pro:A low or dead enemy mid makes the river yours

when: you are behind their mid in level and CS
asks: I'm behind should I roam
can I roam to get back in the game
losing lane do I go bot for kills
should I leave lane I'm getting beat
say: Skip the long roam while you're down levels; farm the wave, or move only when a fight starts right beside mid.
more: A roam from behind stacks two losses. You give up the wave, and you arrive weaker than the people you are trying to kill.
River fights next to your lane are different: the walk is short, and you lose few minions if it goes nowhere.
Two or three clean waves and an item change what you can do far more than a coin-flip visit to a side lane.
check: Whether the wave lets you farm safely, and whether a fight near mid already has your jungler in it.
breaks: If their mid is the one roaming and your side lane is about to be dived, go anyway. Showing up can be enough to stop it.

when: you just reached level 6 and the enemy bot laners are below level 6
asks: I'm six now should I roam
I got my ult do I go bot
level six what do I do
do I use my ult on a roam
say: Level 6 is your window: crash this wave and look bot before they get their ultimates, or use it on their mid if he's low.
more: Solo lanes level faster than the duo lane, so for a short time you carry an ultimate into a lane that has none.
That gap closes within a couple of waves, so the roam is worth more now than it will be in two minutes.
If their mid is still level 5 and hurt, the kill in your own lane is closer and costs no minions.
check: The levels of both bot laners, whether they are pushed up, and whether your wave is going into their tower.
breaks: If bot is pinned under its own tower you would be walking into a dive without a wave. Use the ultimate in mid or with your jungler in river.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: when do I ult as TF
should I Destiny bot
where do I use my ult
do I roam with ult or hold it
who do I ult to
say: Shove the wave, then Destiny onto a lane that's pushed past the middle, or hold it to answer their jungler's next gank.
more: Destiny shows every enemy champion, so cast it when you need to know where their jungler is, even if you never use Gate.
Pick a Card before you land, so the card you want is ready the moment you arrive.
Used on a counter-gank, it turns a two against two into three against two with no walking time for them to react to.
check: Which lanes are pushed toward your towers, and whether your mid wave is shoved so you lose little while away.
breaks: If you are behind their mid, a Gate into a fight you cannot win only gives them a kill. Use Destiny for the vision and stay.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: when do I ult as Galio
should I ult bot
do I hold Hero's Entrance
where do I use my ult
how do I roam as Galio
say: Keep the wave pushed and drop Hero's Entrance on the first ally who gets jumped, or walk to river with your jungler when nobody is fighting.
more: Hero's Entrance shields allies where you land and knocks up enemies around them, so it is strongest as the answer to their engage, not as the opener.
A pushed wave is what makes it free. If your wave is under your tower, the ultimate costs you a wave and plates.
Tell your side lanes you have it. They can take a fight they would normally refuse, and that changes how the whole lane plays.
check: Where the fights are starting, and whether your ally will survive the delay before you land.
breaks: If the ally is already dead or the enemies have left by the time you land, you arrive alone. Hold it and walk instead.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: when do I use wall as Taliyah
should I ult to bot
how do I roam on Taliyah
do I wall or walk
where do I ult
say: Crash the wave, then surf Weaver's Wall toward a side lane so you arrive early, or keep it to cut the river in a fight.
more: The wall gets you there before their mid can follow on foot, so the lane you visit has an extra player for a short while.
Laid across a river path, it also splits their team: whoever is on the wrong side cannot join the fight in time.
Unraveled Earth on their escape route makes anyone who dashes through it pay, which suits a gank from behind.
check: Whether your wave is crashed, and which way the enemy would run when you arrive.
breaks: If their side lane has already backed off, the wall is wasted. Walk to river and save it for the next objective fight.

asks: how do I roam as Talon
should I go bot as Talon
do I roam or farm Talon
when do I leave lane on Talon
say: Clear the wave with Rake and vault the walls straight to river, or into their jungle if their jungler showed on the other side.
more: Assassin's Path takes you over terrain, so your routes skip the usual warded entrances. Each wall goes on a long cooldown, so plan the way out too.
Your roams arrive faster than their mid can follow, which is why shoving and leaving is the plan and standing in lane is not.
A camp taken from their jungle on the way back means the roam pays even when the lane backs off.
check: Where their jungler was last seen, and which walls you already used on the way in.
breaks: If their mid can shove you under tower every wave, you cannot leave for free. Farm until a wave lets you crash it.

asks: should I roam as a mage
I'm immobile do I roam
can I leave lane on this champ
do control mages roam
say: Your roam is short: push and step into river beside your jungler, or stay for plates. The long walk to a side lane rarely pays you.
more: You push waves fast but walk slowly and have no escape, so the long roam costs you more than it costs a mobile champion.
Standing in river with a pushed wave already does the job: your jungler can take a crab or invade because you arrive first.
Later, the same wave control gets you to every objective before their mid.
check: Whether the river brushes are warded, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If a side lane fight starts close to river and your wave is already crashed, go; that is still the short roam.

when: before 2:55
asks: should I roam before level six
do I leave lane early
can I help my jungler now
is it too early to roam
say: This early, stay and work the wave so you can move to river at 2:55, or leave sooner only if your jungler is being invaded.
more: Both river crabs arrive at 2:55, so the first useful move for a mid laner is toward one of them with a wave already pushing.
Every minion matters most now, because the first levels decide who wins that river fight.
A fight in your own jungle is the exception: it is close to you, and whoever's mid arrives first usually wins it.
check: Whether your wave is pushing toward them, and your health and mana compared with their mid.
breaks: If their mid has you pushed in, do not walk into river at all. Tell your jungler you cannot move.

when: you left lane and came back with no kill or assist
asks: my roam failed now what
I roamed and got nothing
I wasted time bot what do I do
that roam didn't work
say: Go straight back and catch the wave, then stay for a few waves to recover, or recall first if you can afford an item.
more: One failed roam costs a wave. Two in a row is how a mid laner ends up two levels down with no idea why.
Ask whether a Flash was burned. If it was, tell your jungler; the roam still set up his next gank there.
Next time, leave only on a wave that is already at their tower, and turn back the moment the target retreats.
check: How much farm their mid gained on you, and whether your tower lost plates while you were gone.
breaks: If the side lane you left is still being dived, do not walk away mid-fight. Finish helping, then reset.
basis: pro:Stop repeating a gank that keeps failing

when: you hold enough gold for an item component
asks: should I back then roam
do I recall or go bot
can I roam after I base
where do I go after backing
say: Crash the wave, recall, and walk out through river toward the side lane, or go straight to mid if a big wave is arriving.
more: Leaving from base hides you. Their mid sees an empty lane and cannot tell whether you are buying or already walking bot.
You also arrive with the item, so the fight you join is stronger than one you would have walked to from lane.
The cost is the wave meeting your tower without you, so check its size before you commit to the detour.
check: How big the next wave heading to your tower is, and whether the side lane is pushed up as you leave base.
breaks: If their mid shoved while you were buying, mid comes first. Clear it, then look at the map again.

asks: how do I roam as Kat
do I roam or farm Katarina
when do I leave lane on Kat
should I go bot as Katarina
say: Walk to fights that have already started and arrive on low targets for resets, or stay and shove when both side lanes are healthy.
more: Voracity cuts your cooldowns when someone you damaged dies, so a fight with hurt enemies is worth far more to you than a fresh one.
Arriving second also means their crowd control is already spent, which is what stops Death Lotus.
If nothing is happening, farm is fine; you need items for the mid game more than you need a forced play.
check: Health bars in the side lane, and whether their stuns have been used.
breaks: If the enemies there are full health with crowd control ready, turn around. You have no way to start that fight.

asks: should I roam as Aurelion Sol
do I just farm on Asol
when do I fly bot
do I leave lane on Sol
say: Stay and stack on waves most of the time, or use Astral Flight over the wall when a side lane is fighting close to river.
more: Your abilities grow permanently with Stardust, so time spent hitting waves and champions is the plan, not a delay.
Astral Flight crosses terrain, which makes a short roam cheap. Go, hit what is there, and fly back to the wave.
A Falling Star that lands on several champions in a river fight both stuns and adds Stardust, so objective fights suit you.
check: Whether the wave is shoved before you leave, and whether the fight is still going when you would arrive.
breaks: If the roam would cost two waves, skip it. For you, the farm is worth more than a likely assist.

when: their mid is Twisted Fate, Galio or Taliyah and is level 6 or higher
asks: their mid has a roaming ult what do I do
how do I stop him ulting bot
he keeps ulting my side lanes
can I punish his ult
say: Now he's 6, keep your wave pushed so his ultimate costs him minions and plates, or ping early and hold if you can't push.
more: You cannot keep up with an ultimate that moves him faster than you can walk, so the answer is to make it expensive and to warn your team before it happens.
Each time he leaves, hit the tower. A plate and a wave for every roam keeps you even or better.
Tell your side lanes when he reaches level 6. A lane that steps back is a roam that gets nothing.
check: Whether he has just disappeared from lane, and whether your side lanes are far forward.
breaks: If your side lanes ignore the pings and keep dying, stop taking plates and stand nearer to them, so you can walk in when it starts.

when: before 4:00
asks: my jungler is getting invaded do I help
jungler is pinging for help
do I go to his buff
they're in our jungle should I go
say: Go if your wave is pushing and you're healthier than their mid, or stay and ping him out if you'd arrive second.
more: Early jungle fights are decided by which mid laner gets there first, far more than by the two junglers.
If you arrive second, you walk into two people who have already won the first exchange. That often gives them two kills.
Helping costs you part of a wave. Saving your jungler's buff and his life is worth more than that this early.
check: Where your wave is, where their mid is standing, and how much health and mana you both have.
breaks: If their mid has already left lane toward the fight, you are late. Shove your wave and tell your jungler to give the camp.
basis: pro:An invade ends when the nearest lane arrives

when: your jungler is dead
asks: my jungler died what do I do
do I take his camps
jungler's dead should I cover
who protects our jungle now
say: While he's dead, hold mid and keep the wave near your side, or take his nearest camp only if their jungler would steal it.
more: With your jungler dead, theirs is free to gank or invade, and your lane is the one that reaches both sides of the jungle.
A wave held closer to your tower means you cannot be dived as easily and can step into your own jungle quickly.
A camp that would be stolen is better in your pocket. A camp that is safe should wait for your jungler, who needs it more.
check: Your jungler's respawn timer, and whether their jungler has shown anywhere since the kill.
breaks: If an objective is up and their jungler is on it, do not contest alone. Take mid plates or a wave in exchange.

when: before 2:55
asks: do I help with crab
should I go to scuttle
crab is spawning do I move
jungler wants crab help
do I leave for crab
say: Have your wave pushing by 2:55 and step into river with your jungler, or tell him to take the other crab if you're stuck.
more: Both crabs spawn at 2:55, and whichever jungler has a mid laner beside him usually takes his without a fight.
If you cannot move, saying so early is the useful thing. Your jungler can cross to the other crab, and an even swap is a fine result.
The crab is also vision of the river for the next couple of minutes, which protects your own lane from the next gank.
check: Whether your wave is pushing, which side their jungler is likely on, and whether their mid is already walking.
breaks: If their mid shoved first and is in river, do not follow at half health. Catch the wave and let the crab go.
basis: pro:Take the crab on the side where your lanes can move

when: between 2:55 and about 5:25
asks: their mid went to crab first
he's in river already do I go
I'm late to crab
should I follow him to scuttle
say: Don't walk in second; shove the wave he left so it costs him, or follow only if your jungler is already winning there.
more: Arriving second to a river fight means their abilities are waiting for you while yours are still on the way.
The wave he abandoned is a sure gain: minions die to your tower's side of the lane and he misses them.
There are two crabs in this window, so your jungler can still take the other one while theirs is busy with this one.
check: Your jungler's health, and whether the crab is nearly dead or the fight has only just begun.
breaks: If your jungler is caught and will die without you, go and trade abilities to get him out. Do not chase after that.
basis: pro:Take the crab on the side where your lanes can move

when: you are level 5 and a river fight is starting
asks: should I fight at level five
I'm almost six do I go
do I wait for six before fighting
river fight now or wait for ult
say: If one more wave or the crab gets you level 6, take it and then fight, or go now if they're level 5 too.
more: An ultimate arriving in the middle of a skirmish often decides it, and the crab's experience can be the last bit you need.
Compare levels across the fight, not only in your lane. A level 6 on their side and none on yours is a reason to delay.
Hitting the crab while they zone you still costs them abilities spent away from the fight.
check: Your experience bar, since the coach cannot see how close you are to the level, and whether the crab is alive.
breaks: If the fight will be over before you level, a level 5 body now beats a level 6 body too late. Go.
basis: pro:A crab can be the level that wins the skirmish

when: between about 7:00 and 8:00 and grubs have not been taken
asks: do I go to grubs
should I help with grubs
grubs are spawning what do I do
do I leave mid for grubs
say: Crash a wave just before 8:00 and walk to top river with your jungler, or hold mid for plates if they show up with more.
more: Grubs are one window from 8:00 and never come back, so the push that gets you there first is worth planning a wave ahead.
They pay off only if your team then hits towers, so ask whether your side lanes are in a position to use them.
If the enemy sends three or four, your plates and their abandoned waves are a fair trade for giving it.
check: How many enemies are walking toward the top river, and whether your top laner can move or is stuck under a wave.
breaks: If your jungler is on the bottom side, grubs are not your play. Push mid and help him with dragon.
basis: pro:Price grubs against plates and waves

when: a dragon is alive or spawns within a minute
asks: what do I do for dragon
how do I help with drake
dragon's up where do I stand
should I leave mid for dragon
say: Push mid, then stand in river between the pit and their mid so your jungler can start, or back off if their bot arrives first.
more: Your job is to be the first extra body. A pushed mid wave is what lets you get there before their mid can.
Standing on the path from mid blocks the one player who can reach the pit quickly. That is worth more than hitting the dragon yourself.
Dragons add up over the game, so winning the first ones quietly is how the later ones become soul fights in your favor.
check: Whether both bot lanes can move, and which river brushes are warded.
breaks: If their bot lane is pushed and yours is not, they bring four to your three. Give it and shove mid for plates.
basis: pro:The lane that pushes first moves first

when: their mid is dead or just recalled, and dragon or grubs are alive
asks: their mid is dead do we do dragon
I killed mid can we take drake
mid's gone should we start it
he's dead what objective
say: Call your jungler to start it right now, since nobody of theirs can rotate first, or take plates if he's too far away.
more: A dead mid laner is the same as lane priority, without having to push. The river belongs to you for as long as his timer runs.
Start at once. The window is short, and a slow start gives it back.
If your jungler is across the map, do not try it alone. Plates are the guaranteed version of the same lead.
check: Where your jungler is, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If their jungler and bot lane are already at the pit, the missing mid does not fix the numbers. Take mid tower health.
basis: pro:A low or dead enemy mid makes the river yours

when: your team killed Herald and a dragon spawns in the next minute or two
asks: where do we use herald
should herald go mid
do we drop herald now
herald mid or top
say: Ask for Herald mid just before dragon spawns so they must answer two places, or use it now if their mid tower is nearly down.
more: Herald charging mid forces someone to stop it. Whoever does arrives late to the dragon, or they keep the dragon and lose the tower.
An open mid lane then makes every later objective easier, because their team has to walk around to reach the river.
Push the mid wave with it. Without minions, they kill it before it reaches the tower.
check: Whether your jungler still holds Herald, and whether the mid wave is moving toward their tower.
breaks: If their team is already grouped mid, they kill it for free. Use it in the side lane they left.
basis: pro:Herald in mid before a dragon buys the river

when: their mid outer tower has fallen
asks: we took mid tower what now
their mid tower's down where do I go
what do I do after mid tower
mid's open now what
say: With their mid tower gone, push the wave deep and ward their jungle beside the next objective, or shove the side lane on that side.
more: That tower was their safe route to both rivers. Without it they reach the pit through dark jungle or not at all.
Wards placed now, before the spawn, are what let your team catch whoever walks in first.
Shoving the side lane next to the objective has the same effect from the other direction: someone has to leave to catch it.
check: Which objective spawns next and when, and how many enemies are showing before you step into their jungle.
breaks: If you cannot see at least three of them, do not walk deep alone. Ward the river entrance and wait for your team.

when: your mid outer tower has fallen
asks: we lost mid tower how do I get to dragon
our mid tower's gone what do I do
how do I play without mid tower
can I still go to river
say: Without your mid tower, clear the wave from further back and walk to river with two others, or trade on the other side.
more: The river next to a fallen mid tower is theirs until you ward it again, so walking in alone is how the fight starts four against five.
Clearing the mid wave before you move still matters. A wave at your next tower pulls someone back at the worst moment.
If you cannot get in, start the trade when they start their objective, not after they finish it.
check: Which brushes on your route are warded, and who on your team is close enough to walk with you.
breaks: If their team is already on the objective and yours is scattered, give it. Take a side tower or their camps on the far side.

when: an objective spawns within about a minute and you hold gold for an item
asks: should I back before dragon
do I have time to recall
back now or stay for the objective
can I base before baron
say: Shove one wave and recall now so you arrive with the item, or stay only if recalling would make you late.
more: A recall a minute early means you walk in healthy, with the item, alongside your team.
Recalling at the last second is the worst case. They start the objective while you are still running from base.
If you stay, do not take a risky trade. A death now loses the objective as well as the kill.
check: How long until the spawn, your health and mana, and whether the wave will hold for the time you are gone.
breaks: If the spawn is too close to get back in time, stay, play safe at range and buy afterwards.
basis: pro:Before a spawn, arrive alive and on time

when: their jungler is dead and an objective is alive
asks: their jungler's dead do we take drake
jungler is down what do we do
can we baron their jungler died
should we start it now
say: Their jungler's dead, so drop the chase and start the objective together, or take mid tower if the timer's too short.
more: Without their jungler, nobody on their side has a reliable last hit, so they usually defend waves and do not walk in.
The pit is safer than a chase through their jungle, and it is worth more than one extra kill.
Compare his respawn timer with how long the take will be. If it is close, a tower is the certain reward.
check: His respawn timer, your team's health, and whether your own jungler is alive and close.
breaks: If your jungler is dead as well, an objective race is a gamble. Take towers or reset and buy.
basis: pro:A dead jungler makes the objective free

when: two or more allies are dead and the enemy is at an objective
asks: we can't contest what do I do
should I try to stop dragon
they're taking baron do I go
do I go for the steal
say: Give this one and take something back now: mid plates or tower, their camps, or the other objective if it's alive.
more: Walking in short-handed usually adds kills to the objective they were getting anyway.
The trade has to start when they start, not when they finish, or they get both.
A tower lasts the whole game and opens their jungle for the next spawn, so it is a real answer and not a consolation.
check: How many enemies you can see at the pit, and what you can finish before they rotate back.
breaks: If nothing of similar size is available, clear waves and reset together so you are five for the next one.
basis: pro:If you cannot contest, take something elsewhere at once

when: after 20:00 and Baron is alive
asks: how do we set up baron
what do I do before baron
should I be at baron
do I leave mid for baron
say: Push the mid wave past the river first, then walk to Baron as a group, or stay and hold mid if your team isn't there yet.
more: A mid wave pushing into them forces someone to answer it, so their team reaches the pit a player short or loses the tower.
The player who clears mid fastest should be the one to do it, and that is often you.
Being first into the top river with wards down matters more than starting Baron quickly.
check: Where the three waves are, and whether their jungler is alive and showing.
breaks: If your mid wave is at your own tower, do not leave it. Baron started while a wave crashes into you costs a tower.
basis: pro:Push the side waves before you posture at Baron

when: the enemy team has taken three dragons
asks: they're on soul point what do we do
do we have to fight this dragon
they have three drakes
can we give this one
say: This dragon is the one to fight: recall a minute early and be there first, or trade Baron if it's alive and you can't contest.
more: Four dragons give soul, so this is the last one you can afford to lose. Every earlier concession was buying time for this fight.
Being first with wards is how the weaker team wins it: they have to walk through the dark toward you.
If the fight cannot be won, something large has to come back. A few camps do not match a soul.
check: The spawn timer, who has Teleport, and how far your carries are from their next item.
breaks: If two of your team are dead before the spawn, do not go in three against five. Trade and plan for elder.
basis: pro:Give early dragons, then fight the one before soul point

when: their mid is level 6 and you are level 5, or they finished an item you have not
asks: should we fight for this dragon
can we contest drake
do we give dragon
I'm not six yet do we fight
say: You're a spike behind, so give this dragon and take waves or their camps, or contest only if it's their third.
more: A fight where they have an ultimate or a finished item that you lack is usually lost before it starts.
An early dragon given is cheap. A lost fight costs the dragon, the kills and the next few waves as well.
Use the time: the waves you catch while they take it are what bring you level for the next one.
check: How close you and your carries are to the level or item, and how many dragons they already have.
breaks: If your side lanes are well ahead and already at the pit, your missing level matters less. Go and stay at range.
basis: pro:Do not fight an objective one spike behind

when: an objective is alive or about to spawn
asks: should we start dragon or wait
do we start it or poke
how do I play objectives as a poke champ
do we rush baron
say: Get there first and poke them as they walk in; let them start it, or start it yourselves only when they have no engage.
more: A team hitting an objective is clumped in a small space. That is exactly where an engage team wants you.
Arriving first lets you hit them on the way in, so the fight starts with them already hurt.
If they start it, they are the ones clumped, and every ability you throw into the pit lands.
check: Whether their engage champion is showing and has Flash, and whether the flanks behind you are warded.
breaks: If their engager is dead or has just used his ultimate, the pit is safe for a short time. Start it then.

big wave mid and they're starting drake

do I leave this wave
say: Clear the wave fast and then go if the fight hasn't started, or go straight there if your team is already committed.
more: A wave left at your tower costs gold, experience and tower health. A teammate fighting four against five costs more.
If you clear waves quickly, the detour is a few seconds, and you arrive with the lane pushing for you.
Say what you are doing. A team that knows you are a few seconds late can wait; a team that does not will start without you.
check: How big the wave is, and whether abilities are already being thrown at the pit.
breaks: If you would arrive after the fight is decided either way, stay and take the wave, then look for the trade.

asks: what do I do in teamfights
who do I go on
how do I fight as an assassin
when do I go in
what's my job in fights
say: Come from the side after their main crowd control is used and kill a carry, or take whoever's alone if the carries are protected.
more: You do your job in the two seconds after their stuns are gone. Going first means you take every one of them.
The side angle matters because the carry has to turn away from your front line to deal with you.
A kill on a support or a stray bruiser before the fight is also a win: it makes the fight five against four.
check: Which of their crowd control abilities have been used, and whether the flank you want is warded.
breaks: If they hold everything for you and their carries stand together, do not force it. Guard your own carry and wait for a mistake.

when: their carries have more kills and items than you
asks: I'm behind how do I teamfight
I can't kill their carry what do I do
I do no damage in fights
how do I fight when I'm weak
say: Don't dive the back line from behind; stand by your carry and kill whoever jumps on them, or pick a straggler before the fight.
more: From behind, your burst does not finish a carry who has items, and you die in the middle of their team.
The enemy who dives your carry has already used his abilities and is surrounded by your team, which makes him a kill you can get.
Assists and a won fight bring you back faster than one desperate attempt at their strongest player.
check: Who on their team is the diver, and whether your carry is standing close enough for you to help.
breaks: If their carry is caught alone with no summoner spells, take it. The rule is about fighting through their whole team.

asks: where do I stand in fights
what do I do in teamfights as a mage
how do I teamfight
who do I hit in fights
say: Stand behind your front line and put your zone on the choke they must walk through, or drop it on your carry when divers come.
more: Your abilities own an area. Placed on the only path in, they make their team split or walk through damage.
Hit whoever is closest and safe to hit. Reaching for their back line is how a mage gets caught.
Used defensively, the same abilities keep your carry alive, and that is often worth more than your own damage.
check: Where their divers and flankers are, and which path their team has to take toward you.
breaks: If they have several ways in, do not use everything on one of them. Stay near your carry and react.

asks: do I burst the carry or the tank
who do I use my combo on
how do I teamfight as a burst mage
when do I use my ult in fights
say: Look for a pick before the fight so it starts five on four, or hold your burst for whoever dives your carry.
more: Your damage comes all at once, so the best use is before the fight, on someone who stepped up to ward or clear a wave.
Once the fight is on, the target you can reach safely is usually the one coming at you.
Spending the full combo on a tank leaves you with nothing while their damage dealers are still alive.
check: Who is walking alone, and which of them has Flash according to what you have seen.
breaks: If their carry walks into your range without Flash, take that over everything else.

asks: how do I teamfight as a poke champ
do I go in or stay back
where do I stand with long range
what's my job in fights
say: Poke from max range until one of them is too low to fight, then call the engage, or give ground if they close on you first.
more: Your fight happens before the fight. A team with one member at half health has to leave or play four against five.
Stay at your own range and not your team's. You are the easiest kill on the map once someone reaches you.
Giving ground costs little. They have to cross your abilities again to get back to where they were.
check: Your mana, the health of their front line, and whether a flank behind you is warded.
breaks: If they engage while you are caught in front, stop poking. Use everything on the nearest enemy and walk back toward your team.

asks: where do I put the ball
who do I ult as Orianna

more: Command: Protect rides the ball on an ally and shields them, so your engager carries your ultimate into their team for you.
Command: Shockwave pulls enemies toward the ball, which bunches them for the rest of your team's abilities.
Command: Dissonance afterwards speeds allies and slows enemies, so drop it on the same spot to keep the fight where you want it.
check: Who on your team is about to engage, and who on theirs is aiming for you.
breaks: If your engager is not going in, do not send the ball forward alone. Keep it close and use it on whoever reaches you.

asks: who do I ult as Zed
when do I go in on Zed

do I ult the ADC

more: Death Mark makes you untargetable as you go in, so it also dodges one ability if you time it against their crowd control.
The mark repeats part of the damage you dealt, so hold your shurikens and slash until you can land them all inside it.
Place the shadow before you ult. Then your way out is already there when the mark pops.
check: Which of their protective abilities and summoner spells have been used, and where your shadow can safely sit.
breaks: If their carry has a stasis item or a guardian next to him, mark someone else or poke with shurikens from the shadow.

asks: when do I go in as Kat
how do I teamfight Katarina
do I ult right away
who do I jump on as Kat
say: Wait outside until their crowd control is used, then Shunpo onto low targets for resets, or throw daggers and stay out if they hold a stun.
more: Death Lotus is a channel, so one stun or knock-up ends it. Count their crowd control before you enter.
Voracity cuts your cooldowns when a champion you damaged dies, so starting on the lowest target gets the chain going.
Coming in late feels slow, but the end of the fight is where you do your work.
check: Which stuns, knock-ups and silences you have seen go out, and who is low.
breaks: If they have too much crowd control to count, play the edges all fight and clean up only once it is clearly won.

asks: when do I ult as Azir
do I shuffle or hold ult

what's my job as Azir
say: Hold Emperor's Divide to shove divers off your carries, or dash in and knock a carry back into your team when they're clumped.
more: Emperor's Divide knocks enemies back, so it protects your back line just as well as it starts a fight.
Most of your damage is soldiers attacking from range, so in an ordinary fight you plant them and stay behind your front line.
The dash-in play wins fights outright, but it leaves you inside their team. Take it when the reward is a carry.
check: Who their divers are, whether your Flash is up, and whether their carries are standing together.
breaks: If you are your team's only steady damage, do not dash in. Keep the ultimate for whoever reaches you.

more: Frozen Tomb on an enemy is a stun your team can pile onto. Ring of Frost roots everyone around you when you arrive.
Cast on yourself, it makes you untargetable and heals you, so you can be the one who goes in first and still survive.
Decide before the fight which use you want, because pressing it in a panic usually wastes both.
check: Whether your team is close enough to follow, and who on their side can lock you down.
breaks: If your team is poking or kiting backwards, do not go in. Use the root and the ultimate on whoever chases.

asks: where do I put my W as Viktor
how do I teamfight on Viktor
who do I ult as Viktor

say: Drop Gravity Field on the choke and sweep Hextech Ray through the pack, or hold the field for whoever dashes at you.
more: Gravity Field slows and then stuns enemies who stay inside, so in a narrow path it forces them to stop or go around.
Arcane Storm can be moved after you cast it. Start it on the nearest threat, then steer it to follow the fight.
You have no dash, so the field is also your only protection. Using it forward means trusting your team to guard you.
check: Which of their champions can reach you, and whether the fight is in a narrow path or open ground.
breaks: Against several divers, keep the field at your feet and fight from inside it.

more: Crystallize blocks movement for a short time, so a team walking through a jungle path can be cut in two.
Glacial Storm slows and damages an area. On the only way in, it works as a wall they can cross but would rather not.
Frostbite hits much harder on targets inside a full storm or hit by Flash Frost, so use it on whoever is already slowed.
check: Where the narrow paths are around the fight, and how much mana you have left.
breaks: In open ground the wall splits nobody. Keep it to block a diver's path to your carry.

asks: where do I cage as Veigar
who do I ult as Veigar

more: Event Horizon stuns anyone who crosses its edge, so placed on a path it stops an engage or traps the front half of their team.
Primordial Burst does more to targets that are already missing health, so it is a finisher and not an opener.
Every spell that hits a champion adds to your power for good, so long poke phases suit you.
check: Who has dashes that cross the cage, and whose health is already low.
breaks: If their team will not walk into the cage, use it defensively. A cage around your own back line makes diving expensive.

more: Fate Sealed pulls everyone it hits toward you, so one good line can bunch their team for your whole side.
Soul Unbound returns you to where you started and repeats part of your damage, which lets you go in without committing.
You are a sustained fighter more than a burst one. Staying alive on their front line for a long fight is a fine outcome.
check: Whether your team can follow the ultimate, and how much time Soul Unbound has left before it pulls you back.
breaks: If nobody follows, you are alone in the middle of their team. Without your team nearby, use the spirit form to trade and wait.

asks: when do I go in as Akali
how do I teamfight on Akali
who do I ult as Akali
do I use shroud first
say: Go in with Perfect Execution on a squishy after their crowd control, and wait in Twilight Shroud between combos, or stay wide for stragglers.
more: Inside the shroud you cannot be selected by attacks or targeted spells, so it buys time for your abilities to come back.
The second cast of Perfect Execution hits hardest on low targets. Hold it to finish, not to open.
Attacking from the shroud reveals you briefly, so there are moments when standing still is right.
check: Which of their abilities can still hit you inside the shroud, and who is isolated.
breaks: If they stack on top of each other, there is no squishy to isolate. Poke with Five Point Strike until someone drops low.

asks: whose ult do I take as Sylas
who do I Hijack
how do I teamfight on Sylas
which ult is best to steal
say: Hijack their best team-fight ultimate before the fight and go in behind your tank, or take a burst ultimate when one carry must die.
more: Hijack lets you cast an enemy's ultimate, so look at their team and decide which one would hurt them most in your hands.
Take it before the fight starts. Reaching for it in the middle of one puts you in range of everything.
Kingslayer heals you against champions, so short repeated trades on their front line favor you while you wait to use what you stole.
check: Which enemy ultimates are available to take, and whether you can reach that champion safely.
breaks: If the ultimate you want belongs to someone standing at the back, take the closest useful one. A good one now beats a perfect one never.

asks: who do I ult as Malz
do I ult the carry or the diver

say: Nether Grasp whoever dives your carry so your team kills him, or grab their carry only when your team is close enough to finish.
more: Nether Grasp holds one champion still and takes him out of the fight for as long as you channel, but you are standing still too.
Void Shift soaks the first hit while it is up, so step forward with it intact and you will often get the channel off.
Malefic Visions keeps dealing damage for as long as your other spells refresh it. Cast it early and keep it going.
check: Who can interrupt your channel, and whether your team is in range of the target you want.
breaks: If their team has plenty of ways to interrupt you, treat the ultimate as peel only and use it from behind your front line.

more: The fish sticks to the champion it touches and slows them before the knock-up, so a hit from range starts the fight on your terms.
Playful makes you untargetable. Used on the way in it adds damage; saved, it dodges the one ability that would kill you.
You cannot do both. Decide by whether they have a single ability you must avoid.
check: Whether the path to their carry is clear for the fish, and which of their abilities you most need to dodge.
breaks: If the fish hits a tank, do not follow it in. Wait for your abilities and look for a flank on the next fight.

asks: who do I ult as Syndra
where do I stun as Syndra

more: Scatter the Weak pushes your spheres into enemies to stun them, so set a sphere down first and your stun reaches much further.
Unleashed Power throws every sphere you have at one champion. More spheres on the ground means more damage, so cast Dark Sphere before it.
You have no dash, so the stun is your escape as well as your opener. You rarely get both from one cast.
check: How many spheres are out, and which of their champions is coming for you.
breaks: If their carry stays out of range, do not walk forward for it. Use the ultimate on whoever you can reach and finish.

asks: how do I teamfight as Ahri
when do I charm
do I ult in or save it
who do I go on as Ahri
say: Start with Charm on anyone squishy and call it, or keep Spirit Rush to dodge and kite when they're diving you.
more: Charm stops dashes and walks the target toward you, so one hit before the fight is a pick your whole team can follow.
Spirit Rush has three casts and gains more on takedowns. One to get in, one to dodge and one to get out is a sound split.
If the fight is going well, the extra casts let you chase. If it is going badly, they are how you leave.
check: Whether minions or a tank are blocking the Charm, and who on their team can lock you down.
breaks: If the Charm misses, do not ult in after it. Back up and wait for the next one.

asks: when do I ult as Vex
how do I teamfight on Vex
who do I go on as Vex
do I hold fear
say: Hold your fear for whoever dashes at your team, or open with Shadow Surge on a carry when your team is ready to follow.
more: Doom 'n Gloom makes your next basic ability fear and interrupt dashes, so against a diving team you are the answer if you wait.
Shadow Surge marks a champion and lets you dash to them. That is a long-range engage, but it puts you in the middle of their team.
Personal Space shields you and hits everything nearby, so use it as you land.
check: Whether your empowered fear is ready, and how many of their champions rely on dashes.
breaks: If their team has no dashes, the fear is just crowd control. Use it early and play as a burst mage.

when: an ally is dead and all five enemies are alive

should we fight four v five

say: You're a player down, so clear waves under tower until the respawn, or trade a side tower if they all went to an objective.
more: Most fights a player down are lost before they start. The respawn timer tells you exactly how long to stall.
Wave clear is your contribution here. A team that cannot push into your tower cannot use its numbers.
If they turn to an objective, they are no longer watching towers, and that is the opening for a trade.
check: The ally's respawn timer, and where the enemy team is showing.
breaks: If one of them is caught alone and far from the others, the numbers are even for that moment. Take the pick and back off.

when: you have more kills, CS or levels than their mid

say: Spend the lead on the map: shove and move with your jungler to the next objective, or take plates when nobody can be reached.
more: A lead that stays in mid lane helps only you. Moved to a river or a side lane, it helps three or four people.
Your stronger shove is the tool. You choose when both mid laners leave lane, and you arrive first.
Plates are the fallback, and each one also brings their tower closer to falling, which opens the map for later.
check: Which objective is next, where your jungler is, and whether their jungler has shown.
breaks: If you are ahead but their jungler keeps coming mid, stop pushing without vision. Ward first, then shove.

when: you killed their mid in the last 30 seconds
asks: I got a kill now what
I just killed him do I back
should I push after the kill
kill mid what next
say: Crash the wave into his tower so he loses it, then recall and spend, or take a plate first if you're healthy.
more: A kill is worth more when the wave dies to his tower while he is gone. Then he is behind in gold and in experience.
Recalling straight after turns the gold into an item before he is back. That is what makes the next fight easier.
If you stay too long on low health, their jungler takes the kill back along with your bounty.
check: Your health and mana, the size of the wave, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If the wave is stuck on your side and you cannot crash it, recall at once. A slow push lost is better than dying for it.
basis: pro:Kills are not a lead if the farm went the other way

when: you have more kills and items than their mid
asks: I'm fed as an assassin what do I do
how do I carry from here
I'm ahead how do I end
who do I kill now
say: Your lead fades as they buy defense, so hunt a pick before each objective now, or push a side lane and kill whoever answers.
more: An assassin's lead has a clock on it. Carries finish defensive items and group, and then the same combo no longer kills.
A pick just before a spawn turns into the objective. A pick at a random moment turns into a wave or two.
In a side lane they have to send someone to stop you. If you beat that person alone, they have to send two.
check: When the next objective spawns, and who on their team is walking alone.
breaks: If they move as five and never show alone, stop hunting. Push side waves and make them choose between you and the objective.

when: you have more CS and items than their mid
asks: I'm ahead as a mage what do I do
how do I use my lead on a mage
I out-farmed him now what

say: Take their mid tower with your wave clear and be early to the next objective, or shove a side wave first if mid is open.
more: Your lead shows up as waves that vanish. Use that on mid first, because their mid tower guards both rivers.
With mid open and the wave pushing, you reach every objective before their mid laner.
You do not need solo kills. Arriving first with full mana, every time, is how a mage lead wins games.
check: Their mid tower's health, and how long until the next objective spawns.
breaks: If their assassin or jungler is hunting you, stay with a teammate. Your lead ends the moment you are caught alone.

when: you are holding enough gold for a full item

do I spend or keep pushing

back or stay
say: That gold does nothing in your pocket: recall on the next crash and buy, or finish an objective first only if it's already started.
more: A gold lead is not an item lead until you spend it. You can be ahead on paper and lose the fight on old items.
Crash the wave before you go, so the recall costs you as few minions as possible.
Buying before the next spawn matters more than buying after it.
check: The wave's position, and how long until the next objective.
breaks: If your team is in a fight right now, the fight comes first. Recall the moment it ends.
basis: pro:A lead is not power until it is spent

when: your team has more kills and towers than theirs

say: You're ahead, so hold waves and vision and let them walk into you, or take the kill only if he's alone and the others are showing.
more: The team that is behind needs you to make one mistake. A chase into dark jungle is the usual one.
Waves and wards cost nothing and tighten the map each minute. The lead grows without any risk.
The kill is optional. The lead is what you must keep.
check: How many enemies you can see on the map, and whether your team is close enough to follow.
breaks: If the target has no escape and four of his team are visible elsewhere, the kill is safe. Take it and go straight to an objective.

when: your team got two or more kills in the last 30 seconds

say: Don't chase the last one: take mid tower with the wave, or peel off to catch the side wave if the others can finish it.
more: Kills pay only when they turn into a tower, an objective or a clean recall. A chase gives none of those.
One player on the side wave means their respawns do not come back to a free push into your tower.
Look at the death timers. Long ones mean an objective; short ones mean a tower and then out.
check: Their respawn timers, where the side waves are, and your team's health.
breaks: If your team is too low to take anything safely, recall together and spend the gold. That still turns the fight into something.

when: your team has more kills, and their carries are scaling champions

say: Turn the kills into dragons before their items arrive by being first to every spawn, or take towers when they won't contest.
more: Against a team that wants a quiet game, dragons are the clock. Each one brings forward the fight they have to take.
Kills alone are a thin lead. Gold from kills fades as the game goes on, and dragon stacks and towers do not.
If they give objectives without a fight, the answer is more objectives. Do not dive them under tower.
check: The dragon count on both sides, and how close their carries are to their main items.
breaks: If you cannot break their towers and they clear every wave, set up for soul. Do not force a dive.
basis: pro:Early dragons are the clock against a scaling team

when: you are level 6 and their mid is level 5

say: You have the level, so fight him now or pull your jungler into a river skirmish, or shove and take the ultimate to a side lane.
more: A level lead is real power right away: more stats and an ultimate he cannot match.
It lasts about a wave, so the choice has to be made now and not after one more recall.
If he backs off to his tower, you have still won something. He misses minions and you get the push.
check: His health, whether he has Flash, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If their jungler is likely nearby and you have no vision, take the safe version: shove the wave and move with the ultimate.
basis: pro:Early on, a level is worth more than a little gold

when: you are ahead of their mid, but your team has fewer kills and towers
asks: I'm fed but my team is losing
how do I carry a losing team
I'm ahead and we're behind
my team is feeding what do I do
say: Be at every objective with them, since they can't fight without you, or push a side wave only when nothing spawns soon.
more: When you are the only strong player, your absence decides fights. An objective fought without you is usually lost.
Your death is their best way to end the game, so walk with someone and keep to warded paths.
Use the quiet time between spawns for side waves. That keeps your gold coming without missing a fight.
check: The next objective timer, and how many enemies are showing before you step into a side lane.
breaks: If your team fights without you regardless, stay close to them. Farm the mid wave and the nearby camps.

when: you have died to their mid and trail in level and CS

say: Give the plates and farm what reaches your tower; don't trade until you have an item, or ask for a gank if he's pushed up.
more: From behind, every trade goes his way. The aim is to stop the gap growing and to take the gold that comes to you.
A wave under your tower is safe farm, and it leaves him pushed up where your jungler can find him.
An item and a level change the lane more than any outplay will.
check: Whether the wave is coming to you, and whether your jungler is near enough to use his position.
breaks: If he can dive you under tower with his jungler, farming there is not safe either. Give the wave and stay out of range.

when: you have fewer kills and items than their carries

how do I get back in as an assassin

say: You can't kill a carry yet, so go for their support or whoever's lowest, or catch side waves until your next item.
more: An assassin who is behind still kills supports and players already at half health, and those kills win fights too.
Side waves are the quiet way back. One finished item can restore your ability to kill a squishy.
The mistake is trying to prove you can still do your job on their strongest player.
check: Who on their team has the least health and fewest defensive items, and how many enemies are showing before you go side.
breaks: If their team hunts side lanes, stay with your team and take assists.

when: you have fewer kills and items than their mid

say: Be the wave clear: hold mid tower by killing waves from range, or stand behind your team and just land crowd control.
more: Wave clear does not depend on being ahead. A team that cannot push into you cannot end the game.
Your crowd control works the same at any gold total. Landing it on their diver is a full contribution.
Each wave you clear safely is also your way back, so defending and catching up are the same job.
check: Your mana, and whether anyone on their team can reach you over the wave.
breaks: If they dive past the wave anyway, stand further back and give tower health. Do not give a kill.

when: their mid has more kills and levels than you

say: Don't follow a stronger mid into river; ping it, push, and take plates, or stay back entirely if their jungler hasn't shown.
more: Following a mid who beats you just gives him a second target on the way.
The ping is the important part. A side lane that backs off turns his roam into lost minions for him.
Plates taken while he is away are how a losing lane gets back to even without winning a single trade.
check: Whether your side lanes reacted to the ping, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If their jungler is missing as well, the empty lane may be bait. Farm near your tower and do not push.

when: your team has fewer kills and towers than theirs
asks: we're losing what do I do
how do we come back
my team is behind
can we still win this
what do I do when we're losing
say: Stop taking even fights; catch every side wave you safely can and defend towers as five, or fight only when one of them is caught.
more: The team ahead wants fights. The team behind wants time, waves and a single mistake to punish.
Wave gold is the comeback nobody can deny you, as long as you do not die collecting it.
Comebacks start with a pick. One of them alone in your jungle or on a side wave is the fight to take.
check: How many enemies are showing before you walk to a side wave, and which of your towers is under threat.
breaks: If they are about to take soul or Baron, waiting is over. That is the fight you have to show up for.
basis: pro:Give early dragons, then fight the one before soul point

asks: I'm behind on a scaling champ
is it fine to just farm
do I need to fight early
I'm weak early what do I do
say: On a scaling champion a quiet early game is the plan: take every wave and give early dragons, or join only fights beside your tower.
more: You are measured against your own item timings, not against their mid's kill count.
Early dragons are affordable to give. Soul point is not, so count them.
Fights next to your tower are the exception, because the walk is short and the wave comes to you afterwards.
check: Your CS compared with the game time, and how many dragons they have.
breaks: If your team is being dived over and over, pure farming loses the game before you scale. Stand near them and clear waves there.
basis: pro:Give early dragons, then fight the one before soul point

when: you are below level 6
asks: how do I survive lane as Kassadin
I'm getting bullied on Kass
do I just farm as Kassadin
what do I do before six on Kass
say: Against a mage, lean on Void Stone and last-hit with Null Sphere until Riftwalk, or give minions when it's a physical lane.
more: Void Stone cuts magic damage, and Null Sphere adds a shield against it, so mage poke hurts you less than it looks.
Neither helps against physical damage. In those lanes experience matters more than gold, and standing near the wave is enough.
Riftwalk changes the lane. With it you can dodge, chase and roam, so the job until then is to arrive at it alive.
check: Whether their damage is magic or physical, and your health before stepping up for a minion.
breaks: If their jungler camps you before 6, give even more. Dying resets everything you saved.

when: their mid is an assassin with more kills than you
asks: their assassin is fed what do I do
he one shots me
how do I play against a fed Zed
I keep getting picked
say: He wants you alone, so walk with a teammate and skip unwarded side lanes, or farm mid under tower where diving costs him.
more: A fed assassin wins by finding you one at a time. Standing next to someone with crowd control takes that away.
His lead fades if he gets no kills. Each minute you stay alive, your team's items catch up to his.
In fights, stand where he has to go through your front line to reach you.
check: Where he was last seen before you step past the river, and which teammate can peel for you.
breaks: If your team splits up and leaves you, stay under a tower and clear. Do not follow them into the dark.

when: you just respawned
asks: I just respawned where do I go
I died where should I go now
back from dead what do I do
which lane do I go to
say: Go to the wave that's about to hit a tower first, or straight to your team if an objective spawns within a minute.
more: After a death, the fastest recovery is the largest wave you can reach safely.
An objective takes priority, because arriving late costs your team the fight and not just your farm.
Buy before you leave. Gold unspent after a death is a second loss.
check: Where the waves are, and what the objective timers say.
breaks: If your team is already fighting, do not run in one at a time. Clear the nearest wave and join when they regroup.

when: your team is behind and an enemy just died
asks: we got a pick do we fight
one of them is dead what do we do
can we do something now
they're down one should we go
say: That death is your window: group and take the nearest tower or objective while they're four, or reset and buy if you're low.
more: From behind, a numbers advantage is the only time a fight or an objective is on fair terms.
Pick the closest reward. A long walk uses up the timer.
If their jungler is the one who died, an objective is the best reward on the map.
check: The respawn timer, who died, and your team's health.
breaks: If the dead player is their weakest and their strongest are waiting at the objective, take a tower on the other side.
basis: pro:A dead jungler makes the objective free

when: an outer tower has fallen, or it is after about 14:00
asks: do I stay mid or go side
where do I go after laning
should I swap to a side lane
which lane am I in now
do I leave mid now
say: Let your bot lane hold mid and take a side lane for the farm, or stay mid if you're the team's main wave clear.
more: Mid is the shortest and safest lane, so it suits the players who die most easily. That is usually the duo.
Side lanes hold more gold and experience for one person. A mid laner who stays mid all game shares farm three ways.
Go to the side where the next objective is, so you can walk to it.
check: Which objective spawns next, and whether your bot lane is actually moving mid.
breaks: If nobody else can clear the mid wave, stay. A lost mid tower costs more than the side farm gains.

when: Teleport is not in your summoner spells
asks: which side lane do I take
top or bot side
where do I farm mid game
which lane without teleport
say: Take the side lane next to the next objective so you can walk to the fight, or the far one only when nothing spawns soon.
more: Without Teleport, distance is the whole cost of being in a side lane. The near lane keeps you one short walk away.
Push the wave past the river before the spawn and then leave. The wave keeps working while you are at the pit.
The far lane is for quiet periods. Take the farm and come back before the timer.
check: The objective timers, and how many enemies are showing.
breaks: If your team starts a fight while you are on the far side, do not run across the map. Push the tower so the trade is real.

when: Teleport is in your summoner spells
asks: I have teleport where do I split
should I split with TP
which lane do I push with teleport
do I TP to the fight
say: Push the lane away from the objective and Teleport in when the fight starts, or walk over early if Teleport is on cooldown.
more: A far-side push makes them send someone a long way from the pit. Teleport gets you back faster than he can walk.
The result is a fight where you arrive and he does not.
Using Teleport to return to lane a minute before a spawn gives that edge away.
check: Whether Teleport is actually ready, since the coach sees only that you took it, and how long until the spawn.
breaks: If it is on cooldown, play as if you never had it. Take the lane beside the objective.
basis: pro:Teleport decides who has the extra player

asks: how do I side lane as an assassin
do I split as an assassin
should I push side or look for picks
where do I go as an assassin mid game
say: Push the side wave past the river and then vanish into their jungle so they must guess, or walk toward mid for a pick.
more: A pushed wave with nobody visible behind it is a problem for them. Whoever comes to clear it may be walking into you.
You do not need to hit the tower. Being missing is the pressure.
Time it before an objective and they must clear the wave and worry about you in the same half minute.
check: How many enemies are showing, and whether their jungle entrances are warded against you.
breaks: If they send two to clear the wave, do not fight. Leave, and your team has a player advantage somewhere else.

asks: can I side lane as a mage
is it safe to push side
how far do I push the side wave
I have no escape can I split
say: Push the side wave to the river and come back, or go further only when you can see four of them elsewhere.
more: With no dash, your safety is the map. Every enemy you cannot see might be in the brush beside you.
The river is far enough. The wave then pushes on its own and still pulls someone to answer it.
Clear quickly and leave, because your team needs your wave clear at mid again within moments.
check: How many enemies are visible, and whether the river brush on your side is warded.
breaks: If their assassin or jungler is missing, stop at your own tower. The extra minions are not worth a death timer.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: should I split as TF
how do I side lane on Twisted Fate
do I hold ult while splitting
where do I push as TF
say: Push a side lane and keep Destiny to rejoin when the fight starts, or use it to catch whoever comes alone to stop you.
more: Destiny lets you be in a side lane and at the fight within moments, so your team is never truly a player short.
It also shows where all five of them are, which tells you whether the push is safe before you go deeper.
Wild Cards clears waves from range, so you can shove and step back without ever being near the tower.
check: Whether Destiny is ready, and where your team is standing.
breaks: If Destiny is on cooldown you are an immobile mage in a side lane. Push to the river and return.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: how do I split as Ryze
do I use Realm Warp to escape
should I side lane on Ryze
what do I use Ryze ult for
say: Push a side lane and keep Realm Warp as your way out, or bring your team through it for a flank at the objective.
more: Realm Warp moves you and nearby allies a short distance after a delay, so it is an escape you start early and not a panic button.
As a flank, it puts your whole team behind theirs at a pit, where they are clumped and facing the wrong way.
Rune Prison roots a target marked by Spell Flux, which is how you stop whoever comes to answer your push.
check: How many enemies are showing, and whether you can channel the portal without being interrupted.
breaks: If they have several stuns nearby, the portal will be cancelled. Leave on foot before they arrive.

asks: two of them are coming for me
they sent two to stop me
should I keep pushing they're collapsing
do I back off
say: If two come for you, back off and ping your team to take something four on three, or stay only if the tower is almost dead.
more: Two players sent to you is the split working. The reward is collected by your team, not by you.
Dying turns that advantage into a kill for them and a free objective afterwards.
Ping the objective or tower you want them to take. A team that is not told often just stands there.
check: Which two are coming, your escape route, and what your team can reach right now.
breaks: If your team is not in a position to take anything, retreat earlier. Then the split has cost them only walking time.

when: after 20:00 and Baron is alive
asks: do I split or group late
should I be side lane or with team
late game where do I go
do I push side before baron
say: Shove a side wave past the river and then walk to Baron before they see you leave, or stay grouped if your team will fight anyway.
more: A side wave pushing into them means someone has to leave, so their team reaches the pit short or loses a tower.
The wave does the work. You do not need to stay with it.
Late-game death timers are long, so being caught in the side lane can cost Baron and more.
check: Where the side waves are, how many enemies are showing, and whether your team is waiting or about to engage.
breaks: If your team cannot hold four against five for even a few seconds, be with them. Push the mid wave in place of the side wave.
basis: pro:Push the side waves before you posture at Baron

when: you have more kills and items than whoever would answer you
asks: can I split on this champ
should I duel in the side lane
do I split or group
I win the one v one do I stay side
say: If you beat whoever they send, stay side and make them send two, or group when their answer beats you alone.
more: A side lane is a question: who will you send? If their answer loses to you, they lose a tower or a second player.
Check the matchup honestly each time items change. A duel you won at one item can flip at two.
Keep the wave past the river, so the duel happens on their side and near their tower's gold.
check: Who comes to answer, their items compared with yours, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If your team loses four against four without you, the split is costing more than it gains. Join them for objectives.

asks: my top is split pushing what do I do
our top won't group
how do I play with a split pusher
do we fight without top
say: Hold mid with the others and don't start a fight; clear waves until they send someone, or engage once two leave to stop him.
more: With a split pusher your team's job is to not lose four against five while the side lane does the work.
Wave clear at mid is what buys the time, and that is often you.
When two of them go to stop him, you have four against three. That is the moment to take a tower or an objective.
check: How many enemies are in front of you at mid, and how many went to the side lane.
breaks: If all five of them come mid, give ground and clear from range. They are losing a tower on the side for it.

asks: their top is splitting do I go stop him
who answers the split pusher
should I defend the side lane
someone needs to stop their top
say: Go if you clear the wave from range and can't be dived alone, or send your top and hold mid with the team.
more: Answering a split pusher does not mean beating him. Killing the wave from a safe distance is enough.
A mage with wave clear does that well from under tower. A melee champion who loses the duel does not.
If you go, your team is four at mid and must not fight. Tell them.
check: Whether he can dive you under tower, and whether your top laner is able to match him.
breaks: If he has killed whoever answered before, send two, or give the tower and take an objective with all five.
